bypasses_found.input: HEADING_FILES entry inside an accepted docket that is a symlink to a file outside the dockets root (e.g. _smoke/README.md -> ../outside/secret.md)
bypasses_found.why: safe_docket_slug realpath-contains the docket DIRECTORY only. _read_text_capped reads directory/README.md, _headings() extracts markdown headings, and _docket_files lists the symlink (bytes = outside file size). So heading TEXT of an arbitrary outside file is served, and its size disclosed, while the direct path _smoke/README.md is correctly refused by realpath.
bypasses_found.severity: low-moderate: requires local write access to a docket directory (not reachable by URL alone) and the dashboard is loopback-only, but the read routes are unauthenticated on loopback and this is exactly the symlink escape the change exists to prevent.

layers.segment_validation: covers every traversal: separators, '..' anywhere, leading dots, empty/'.'/'...' segments, whitespace-padded segments, all %2f/%2e/%252e/%c0%ae/%2E forms, NUL, newline, unicode lookalikes, overlong names, backslashes. It is the layer that does the work for 52 of 53 inputs.
layers.realpath_containment: covers only the case segment validation cannot see: a segment that is a legal name but resolves outside the root via a symlink ('escape'). It also catches a direct file path (e.g. _smoke/README.md) that is a symlink out. It does NOT cover symlinks reached from inside an already-accepted docket directory.
layers.redundant_line_pin: not pinnable by any traversal input (POSIX needs a separator for '..' to traverse; the regex rejects separators and the leading-dot check rejects a bare '..'), BUT pinnable by a non-traversal refusal-semantics case: a docket directory named with an internal '..' (e.g. ver..2) is addressable only if api.py:122 is removed. Their honesty that the new tests do not pin the line is correct; 'cannot be pinned by design' would be too strong.

served_vs_disk.recommendation: Leave the gate as-is ('unknown' and absent both mean 'no model mined these'), but stop implying provenance was recorded: either emit producer only when the key exists on disk, or add a sibling boolean (e.g. producer_recorded: false) so a downstream reader can distinguish 'field never written' from 'producer explicitly unknown'. Do not implement in this unit.
